J answered QD3-005: 'First count how many instantiate and restrict lines would move; keep them as ruled until I decide.' My meanwhile (instantiate and restrict rulings stand as written, pairs kept under G4) is what J asks, so no ruling rested on a wrong assumption and none changes. Rules for the count, written before any line is read: (1) Population: instantiate and restrict lines of the eleven closed groups whose latest ruling is a paired elaboration (63) or a particular on one room's evidence (9), by _analysis/d3_qd3005_population.py. Out of the count, each with its reason: specifications (6,771) already are what the clause would give; particulars by construction (229, portability false or the room named in its condition) stay particulars under rule 5 whatever the model states; evidence limits (119) and rejects (110) rest on what the concepts show, not on where a form sits in the model; corrections (18) were accepted because the element as it stood failed in the room, and moves 172 and 173 rest on them, so another element's statement does not undo them; the one modify (R01) is a revised line. (2) Test: G4a's four clauses as amended at D3a-11, with the same reading of 'states it': the form or relation the line adds must be stated in its element's statement or range (clause 1), or in another element's statement or range or an arrow's connection, bound or mechanism (clause 2); a counting or coding rule is ruled by its concepts (clause 3); otherwise it stays (clause 4). A line 'would move' when clause 1 or 2 would make it a specification. (3) Each line is read whole: its fields, my reason and, where the reason does not settle it, its concepts through cite.py. (4) The result is a working file, _analysis/d3_qd3005_count.jsonl, with id, element, op, ruling now, ruling under the clause, the id named and why. Nothing is written to adjudications.jsonl. (5) Also counted: the pairs that would break if a line moves, and the effect on the 10 open-boundary pairs
